title: Biosecurity and clean workflow — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define a cannabis cultivation biosecurity SOP foundation that controls introduction, movement and release of plant-health risk while separating quarantine, sanitation, treatment and quality statuses.

included: tool, cart, bench and surface sanitation
excludedUntilValidated: universal quarantine duration for every pathogen and source risk
claim that visual symptom absence proves clean stock
automatic release after a single negative test regardless of assay/sample context
mixing quarantine, pesticide REI, sanitation state, quality hold or equipment status into one generic release flag

claims.statement: Cannabis production can spread important pathogens and viroids through infected stock plants, vegetative cuttings, contaminated tools or surfaces, water/root-zone pathways and movement of plant material, supporting a layered biosecurity program.
claims.boundary: The relative importance of each pathway depends on the organism, facility and production system; pathway possibility is not proof of a specific transmission event.

claims.statement: Maintaining pathogen-free or pathogen-tested stock material and separating stock/propagation areas from production are core preventive strategies in greenhouse cannabis disease management.
claims.boundary: A stock-plant status is only as strong as the sampling plan, assay, timing, source history and control of re-introduction.

claims.statement: Incoming plant material from external sources warrants risk-based isolation, inspection and appropriate diagnostic testing before unrestricted movement into established clean production areas.
claims.boundary: A single fixed isolation duration should not be universalized across organisms, assay windows, source risks and facility procedures.

claims.statement: HLVd infection can be asymptomatic in cannabis, so visual inspection alone is insufficient to establish clean-stock status when HLVd consequence and source risk justify testing.
claims.boundary: Testing strategy, specimen type, assay method, timing and retest rules require validated facility or laboratory procedures.

claims.statement: Sanitation programs should control tools, equipment, benches, containers, floors and other relevant contact/movement surfaces because residual inoculum can contribute to pathogen persistence and spread.
claims.boundary: Research comparisons of sanitizers do not establish one universal product, concentration or contact time; current label, material compatibility, worker safety and facility validation control operational use.

claims.statement: Biosecurity movement should be directional and status-aware: clean material, suspect material, confirmed affected material, waste, tools and personnel should not share uncontrolled routes that can transfer contamination.
claims.boundary: Exact zone names, gowning steps and routing patterns are facility-specific controls that must match actual layout and risk.

claims.statement: Accurate pathogen or viroid diagnosis can determine whether a finding should trigger isolation, destruction, intensified monitoring, additional testing or another response, so diagnostic evidence should be preserved in the biosecurity record.
claims.boundary: The SOP should not treat an unvalidated in-house test or visual diagnosis as equivalent to a qualified diagnostic result.

claims.statement: Quarantine release should be specific to the risk being cleared and should preserve source identity, testing/inspection evidence, movement history, unresolved findings and authorization for release.
claims.boundary: Expiration of a time period or clearance of one control does not automatically clear other quality, pesticide, sanitation or equipment restrictions.

requiredNewPackageSections: incoming plant-material intake and quarantine record
